notes: Experiment 1 is explicitly described as replicating Medway and Jones (2013). It compares zero versus one check over six stove trials; there is no irrelevant light-bulb control in this experiment. Experiment 1 candidate test A: main effect of trial number on the three metamemory ratings, F (1, 76) = 27.00, p < .001, printed partial eta squared 0.26. Candidate test B: main effect of check number on those ratings, F (1, 76) = 0.90, p = .765, printed partial eta squared 0.001. Preserve this printed F/p pair without correction. Accuracy ANOVA reports only that no effects approached significance (smallest p = .53); this is a minimum across effects, not an identified same-test p. Other metamemory effects have smallest p = .151. These candidates cannot be mapped to assigned rows by their order or by matching numbers. Experiment 1 has 81 recruited and 78 completers, with final checking groups of forty and 38; participant unit, no separately reported model exclusions. N=78 remains a candidate only because the critical test correspondence is unresolved. No N inferred from degrees of freedom. Authors explicitly report successful replication of the no-check/check metamemory findings at study level; that verdict does not establish an individual target test. Original side is an unassigned placeholder, not an original-source availability assessment. PDF pages 2–4 were rendered and inspected for layout; supplied canonical text is the evidence source. Target disposition: The description is blank and locator p. 3 contains multiple Experiment 1 tests: accuracy ANOVA, trial-number main effect, check-number main effect, and other metamemory effects. A page and study number do not identify which effect is assigned.
